evidence.translation_difficulty: Ketiv/qere runs 22 notes in 20 of 154 verses (strategy census, not re-verified here), and the acrostic letter order is pe-then-ayin in chs 2-4 against ayin-then-pe in ch 1, a transmission fact the LXX order does not share. Lexical cruces sit at 1:14 (hapax nisqad, LXX read differently), 3:5 (rosh u-tela'ah), 4:3 (tannin ketiv / tannim qere) and 5:22 (the ki im ending, whose force is disputed). Numbering is identity MT=WEB; no Aramaic.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Five poems of different form: single acrostics (1, 2, 4), a triple acrostic (3: 66 vv in 22 letter-triplets) and a non-acrostic communal prayer (5). Inside them the genre shifts by voice rather than by formula: city lament in the narrator's mouth, Zion's first-person speech (1:12-22; 2:20-22), the geber's individual lament (3:1-18), a wisdom-style hope meditation (3:19-39), communal confession (3:40-47; 5:1-18), apostrophes to the wall/daughter of Zion (2:13-19) and to Edom (4:21-22).
evidence.prophecy: No oracles and no divine speech; the only forward-looking units are the imprecatory petitions 1:21-22 and 3:64-66 and the Edom/Zion apostrophe 4:21-22 ('the cup shall pass to you'), whose edges the acrostic already fixes.
evidence.connections: Deut 28:53-57 curse language behind the cannibalism verses 2:20 and 4:10; the 'no comforter' refrain (1:2, 9, 17, 21) answered by Isa 40:1 nachamu; Jer 9:1 / 14:17 weeping and the 'daughter of my people' idiom shared with 2:11, 3:48, 4:3-10; ch 3 in Job 19:7-8 / Ps 88 idiom (3:7-9); 4:21-22 in the Edom cluster with Obad, Ps 137:7, Ezek 25:12-14; 2 Chr 35:25 associates laments with Jeremiah. None of these cross a poem boundary.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Received differently on authorship and use rather than doctrine: the LXX/Vulgate superscription ascribes the book to Jeremiah while the MT is anonymous; Jewish liturgy reads it on Tisha B'Av and Western Christian liturgy sang it at Tenebrae in Holy Week. The identity of the geber of 3:1 (individual, collective persona, or a Christological figure in patristic reading) is an open reception question the strategy holds as literary uncertainty.

books.boundary_risk: A row seam falling inside a ch-3 letter-triplet or mid-letter in chs 1, 2, 4; mislocating the first Zion-voice turn (1:9c/1:11c interjections vs the full turn at 1:12); attaching 3:19-24 to the wrong side of the lament/hope seam; and treating the PE mark at 5:18 as a poem close when 5:19-22 continues the same prayer.
extra_scrutiny_focus: reversed pe-ayin order in chs 2-4 (letter disclosure per row)
books.uncertainty: The K/Q and letter-order digits are quoted from the Lam strategy's byte census, not re-verified in this pass. Scoring was not softened for the cycle already underway; on my scale Lam sits at the low end of this batch (total 8).

evidence.translation_difficulty: MT Ezekiel runs roughly 4-5% longer than the Old Greek; Papyrus 967 and the Old Latin lack 36:23c-38 and place ch 37 after 38-39, so a block of ch 36 is a variant-attested unit. Ch 1 (the chariot vision) carries doublets and LXX minuses (1:14 absent in LXX; expansions in 1:22-27; hashmal 1:4, 27; 8:2 disputed), and chs 40-48 are dense with disputed architectural terms (ta 40:7ff, atummot 40:16, attiqim 41:15-16, 42:3-5, atsil 41:8). Further cruces: 21:10, 21:15 (me'utah, hapax), 27:19 (me'uzzal), 16:7 (revavah). Numbering diverges in ch 21: MT 21:1-5 = WEB 20:45-49, MT 21:6-37 = WEB 21:1-32 (a crosswalk zone).
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Vision reports (1-3; 8-11; 37:1-14; 40-48), sign-acts (4-5; 12; 24:15-27), extended allegories (15 vine; 16 foundling; 17 eagles inside a riddle-mashal frame 17:2; 19 qinah; 23 Oholah/Oholibah), casuistic disputation in legal form (18; 33:10-20), a seven-nation oracle collection with embedded poems (25-32: laments over Tyre 26:17-18, 27:3b-36, 28:12-19, over Pharaoh 32:2-16), proto-apocalyptic Gog (38-39) and priestly temple torah with measurements, ordinances and land allotments (40-48). Poetry sits inside prose frames without marked seams (19; 27; 28; 32), and 13 date-formulas impose a chronological spine.
evidence.prophecy: Oracular from 3:16 to 39:29 and visionary thereafter; the word-event formula 'the word of YHWH came to me' (about 50x) gives unit onsets, but the long oracles (16: 63 vv; 20: 44 vv; 23: 49 vv) subdivide only by interpretive judgment, and the Gog cycle (38-39: a seven-fold 'thus says the Lord YHWH' chain) and the temple vision (43:1-12 / 43:13ff; 47:1-12 / 47:13ff) have internal boundaries that commentators divide differently.
evidence.connections: Lev 17-26 (Holiness Code) idiom saturates 18, 20, 22, 44-46; 1 <-> Isa 6 <-> Rev 4 (living creatures); 2:8-3:3 scroll-eating <-> Rev 10:9-10; 9:4 mark <-> Rev 7:3; 34 shepherds <-> Jer 23:1-6, Zech 11, John 10; 36:25-27 <-> John 3:5; 37 dry bones and two sticks <-> Hos 6:2, Rev 11:11; 38-39 Gog <-> Rev 20:8-9; 40-48 <-> Exod 25-31 and Rev 21-22 (47:1-12 river <-> Rev 22:1-2); 26-28 Tyre <-> Isa 23; 29-32 Egypt <-> Isa 19, Jer 46; 14:14, 20 name Noah, Daniel and Job; 18:2 proverb = Jer 31:29; 12:22-28 proverb disputation.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Received divergently, reported neutrally: 40-48 is read by dispensational premillennialists as a future literal temple with memorial sacrifices and by amillennial/covenantal readers (and most Catholic and Orthodox commentary) as symbolic or fulfilled in Christ and the Church; 38-39 Gog sits inside end-time schemes for some readers and stands as symbolic for others; 44:2 (the shut east gate) is read as a type of Mary's perpetual virginity in a patristic line (Ambrose, Jerome) and in Orthodox hymnography; 28:12-19 (king of Tyre) is read as the fall of Satan by Origen and Tertullian and as court hyperbole by most modern readers; 37:1-14 served Irenaeus and Tertullian as a proof of bodily resurrection while historical readings take national restoration; 18 figures in discussions of inherited guilt and free will; 16 and 23 are largely omitted from lectionaries for their sexual imagery; ch 1 (merkabah) carried expounding restrictions in Mishnah Hagigah 2:1.

books.boundary_risk: Cutting inside a date-formula unit or across the seven-nation frame of 25-32; splitting an embedded poem from its prose frame (19; 27:3b-36 from 27:1-3a; 28:12-19 from 28:11; 32:2-16 from 32:1); breaking 36:23c-38 (the variant-attested block) or the Gog cycle's oracle chain; mis-seaming the MT/WEB offset zone 20:45-21:32 when WEB and OSHB keys diverge; and subdividing 16, 20, 23 or 40-48 by content without a text signal.
extra_scrutiny_focus: 25-32 seven-nation structure and its embedded laments
books.uncertainty: The MT/LXX length percentage and the list of disputed terms in 40-48 are from memory of the standard apparatus, not re-counted here; if anything the textual density is understated.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Bilingual: Hebrew 1:1-2:4a, Aramaic 2:4b-7:28, Hebrew 8-12 (Aramaic morphology and lexicon across the court tales and ch 7). Two Greek text forms (Old Greek vs Theodotion) diverge widely, and the Greek carries additions (Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three inside ch 3, Susanna, Bel and the Dragon) that shift versification (Greek 3:91 = MT 3:24). Persian and Greek loanwords (the instrument list 3:5, 7, 10, 15: qaytros, psanterin, sumponyah); cruces at 9:24-27 (mashiach nagid; 'shall have nothing' 9:26; 'wing of abominations' 9:27), 8:14 (2,300 evening-mornings), 11:45, 12:2. Numbering diverges twice: MT 3:31-33 = WEB 4:1-3 (MT 4:1 = WEB 4:4) and MT 6:1 = WEB 5:31 (MT 6:2 = WEB 6:1).
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Court tales in third person (1-3, 5-6) and a royal first-person encyclical (4), dream reports with interpretation (2, 4), Aramaic hymnic doxologies embedded in prose (2:20-23; 4:3, 34-35; 6:26-27; 7:9-10, 13-14 in poetic lines), apocalyptic vision reports with angelic interpretation (7; 8; 10-12), a Deuteronomic penitential prayer (9:4-19), the seventy-weeks oracle (9:24-27) and an ex eventu historical survey in prophetic dress (11:2-45). The prose/poetry seams in 2, 4, 6, 7 are unmarked in the Aramaic.
evidence.prophecy: Four-kingdom schemes (2:31-45; 7:1-27), the ram and goat (8), seventy weeks (9:24-27), the kings of north and south running without a break into the time of the end (11:2-12:4) and the closing numbers (12:11-12). Vision/interpretation seams (7:1-14 / 7:15-28; 8:1-14 / 8:15-27; 10:1-11:1 / 11:2ff) exist in the text, but every internal boundary of 11:2-12:4 and of 9:24-27 turns on interpretive judgment.
evidence.connections: 9:2 cites Jeremiah's seventy years (Jer 25:11-12; 29:10); 9:4-19 shares its form with Ezra 9 and Neh 9; 7:13 'one like a son of man' <-> Mark 13:26, 14:62, Matt 24:30, Rev 1:7, 1:13, 14:14; 9:27 / 11:31 / 12:11 'abomination of desolation' <-> Matt 24:15, Mark 13:14, 1 Macc 1:54; 7 beasts <-> Rev 13, 17; 12:1 <-> Rev 12:7; 12:2 <-> John 5:28-29; 2:34-35, 44-45 stone <-> Luke 20:18; 3 furnace <-> Heb 11:34; 10:5-6 <-> Rev 1:13-15; 4 <-> the Nabonidus tradition (4Q242); Ezek 14:14, 20 and 28:3 name a Daniel.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception is divided at several points, reported neutrally: canon (the Greek additions are canonical for Catholic and Orthodox churches, apocryphal for Protestants, absent from the Jewish canon; Daniel stands among the Prophets in Christian Bibles and among the Writings in the Tanakh); date and authorship (sixth-century vs Maccabean composition, a debate running from Porphyry and Jerome to the present); 9:24-27 (messianic chronology in much traditional Christian reading, a future seventieth week in dispensationalism, Antiochus IV in historical-critical reading); 7:13 (individual messiah vs the corporate 'holy ones' of 7:18, 22, 27); the fourth kingdom (Rome vs Greece); 8:14 (the 1844 investigative-judgment doctrine of Seventh-day Adventism); 12:2 as a resurrection proof text; 3:25 'a son of the gods' / 'the Son of God' (KJV) as a Christological reading.

books.boundary_risk: Splitting a vision from its interpretation (7:15-28 from 7:1-14) or a dream from its reading (2:31-45); breaking 9:24-27 from the prayer 9:4-19 that motivates it, or cutting inside 9:24-27; imposing sub-units on 11:2-12:4 by historical identification rather than text signal; seaming the Hebrew/Aramaic switch at 2:4b or the numbering zones 3:31-4:3 and 5:31-6:1 wrongly; and treating deuterocanonical insertion points (after 3:23) as if they were MT/WEB boundaries.
extra_scrutiny_focus: MT 3:31-33 = WEB 4:1-3 and MT 6:1 = WEB 5:31 numbering zones
books.uncertainty: My rubric scores (3,3,3,3,3 = 15) would have made Daniel hard without the owner's naming; the naming is confirmed by the rubric, not echoed. The Greek versification equivalence (3:91 = MT 3:24) is from memory of the Rahlfs/Theodotion numbering and should be checked if Greek keys are ever mapped.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Widely held the most corrupt Hebrew text among the prophets: northern-dialect forms, hapax and broken lines cluster in 4-14 (4:4, 4:18, 5:2, 6:5, 7:4-6, 7:16, 8:10, 9:13, 10:5, 10:9-10, 11:2-4, 11:7, MT 12:1), with the LXX often reflecting a different Vorlage (6:5; 9:13; 11:4; 13:14 as questions vs assertions; MT 14:3 'bulls of our lips' vs LXX 'fruit'). Numbering diverges three times: MT 2:1-2 = WEB 1:10-11 (MT 2:3 = WEB 2:1), MT 12:1 = WEB 11:12, MT 14:1 = WEB 13:16.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Sign-act narratives in third person (1) and first person (3) around the marriage-allegory oracle (2); then 4-14, a run of judgment and salvation oracles without superscriptions or messenger formulas, in which covenant lawsuit (4:1-3), priestly torah polemic (4:4-19), penitential liturgy (6:1-3; 14:2-3), historical retrospects (11:1-4 exodus; 12:2-14 Jacob), lament and a wisdom colophon (14:9) succeed one another with unmarked seams; the unit divisions of 4-14 have no scholarly consensus.
evidence.prophecy: Predictive material is moderate (1:10-11; 2:14-23; 3:4-5; 11:10-11; 13:14; 14:4-8) and nothing is apocalyptic, but the whole of 4-14 is oracular speech whose unit boundaries turn on interpretive judgment because formulaic markers are nearly absent (ne'um YHWH only at 2:13, 16, 21; 11:11). The score reflects boundary indeterminacy under the rubric's own definition, not predictive density.
evidence.connections: 11:1 <-> Matt 2:15; 6:6 <-> Matt 9:13, 12:7; 1:10 and 2:23 <-> Rom 9:25-26, 1 Pet 2:10; 13:14 <-> 1 Cor 15:55; 10:8 <-> Luke 23:30, Rev 6:16; 6:2 in resurrection reception (1 Cor 15:4 'according to the scriptures'); 12:3-4, 12 <-> Gen 25:26, 28:10-22, 32:22-32; 11:8 <-> Deut 29:23 (Admah, Zeboiim); 9:9, 10:9 <-> Judg 19-21 (Gibeah); 1:4 <-> 2 Kgs 9-10 (Jezreel); 4:2 <-> the Decalogue; 2 <-> Jer 2-3, Ezek 16, 23 (marriage metaphor); 8:14 <-> the Amos 1-2 'I will send fire' refrain.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported neutrally: the command to take 'a wife of whoredom' (1:2) is read as literal biography by one line (Augustine, most modern commentary) and as vision or parable by another (Ibn Ezra, Maimonides, Calvin); 11:1 as used in Matt 2:15 is a standing case in typology / sensus-plenior discussion; 6:2 'on the third day he will raise us up' is read as a resurrection prophecy by Tertullian and Cyprian and as covenant restoration by historical readers; 13:14 is rendered as promise (KJV, Vulgate) or as taunting questions (NRSV, NIV), and the choice changes the unit's tone.

books.boundary_risk: Within 4-14 almost any seam is a judgment call, so the risk is imposing a structure (cutting at chapter numbers, or at every 'Ephraim' vocative) that the Hebrew does not signal; splitting the penitential liturgy 6:1-3 from the divine reply 6:4-6; severing 1:10-2:1 (MT 2:1-3) from either ch 1 or ch 2 across the numbering zone; and breaking 11:12-12:1 or 13:16-14:1 at the MT/WEB offset.
extra_scrutiny_focus: 1:10-2:1 / MT 2:1-3 numbering zone and the Jezreel reversal
books.uncertainty: The prophecy score is deliberately driven by boundary indeterminacy; if the consolidator weights predictive density instead, 2 is the alternative reading. Specific LXX Vorlage claims are from memory of the standard apparatus.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Numbering diverges: MT 3:1-5 = WEB 2:28-32 and MT 4:1-21 = WEB 3:1-21 (a whole-chapter zone). Cruces: the four locust terms of 1:4 and 2:25 (gazam, arbeh, yeleq, chasil: species or life-stages); 1:17 with three hapax in one clause (avshu, perudot, megrefotehem); 2:6 parur (also Nah 2:10); 2:20 'the northerner'; 2:23 ha-moreh li-tsedaqah ('early rain in right measure' vs 'the teacher of righteousness', Vulgate doctorem iustitiae); MT 4:11 ushu (hapax); and the tense of 2:18 (waw-consecutive forms read as narrative past or as future promise), which decides where the lament ends.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Call to lament and communal lament (1:2-20), day-of-YHWH theophany with an army that is locust and/or human (2:1-11), call to repentance with a liturgical rubric (2:12-17), oracle of salvation (2:18-27), eschatological Spirit promise (2:28-32) and judgment of the nations with a harvest/vintage scene (3). Seventy-three verses, all poetry, and the seam between the historical plague and the eschatological day is itself the interpretive question.
evidence.prophecy: The day of YHWH (1:15; 2:1-2, 11, 31; 3:14) is the book's spine; 2:28-32 and 3:1-21 are wholly predictive; the locust/army ambiguity of 2:1-11 and the 2:18 tense crux mean the boundary between description and prediction turns on judgment, not on a text signal.
evidence.connections: 2:28-32 <-> Acts 2:17-21 (the Pentecost citation) and 2:32 <-> Rom 10:13; 3:13 (MT 4:13) <-> Rev 14:15-19; 2:1-11 <-> Rev 9:2-11; 2:31 <-> Rev 6:12; 3:10 reverses Isa 2:4 / Mic 4:3; 2:13 = Jonah 4:2 <-> Exod 34:6; 3:16 (MT 4:16) = Amos 1:2 and 3:18 <-> Amos 9:13 (the Joel-Amos seam in the Twelve); 2:32 <-> Obad 17 ('as YHWH has said'); 1:15 <-> Isa 13:6; 2:2 <-> Zeph 1:15; 2:3 <-> Gen 2 / Isa 51:3; 3:4-8 <-> Amos 1:6-10 (Tyre, Sidon, Philistia).
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported neutrally: 2:28-32 is read as fulfilled at Pentecost with continuing prophetic gifts (Pentecostal and charismatic readers) or as fulfilled and closed (cessationist readers), and 'your sons and your daughters' is cited in debates over women's ministry; the Valley of Jehoshaphat (3:2, 12) is a literal future site for dispensational readers and symbolic for others; the locusts have been read as a literal plague, as four empires (Jerome) or as an apocalyptic army; 2:23 is messianic in Targum and Vulgate reception and meteorological in most modern translation.

books.boundary_risk: Placing the pivot at 2:18 (or 2:17 / 2:19) wrongly, which decides whether 2:18-27 is narrated response or promise; splitting 2:28-32 from 3:1-21 or joining them, where the MT chapter break (3/4) and the WEB break (2/3) disagree; cutting the 2:1-11 army unit from 2:12-17; and treating 3:16-21 as fragments so the Joel 3:16 / Amos 1:2 book-seam catchword is lost.
books.uncertainty: The hapax identifications at 1:17 and MT 4:11 are from memory of the lexica; WEB is assumed to follow English chapter numbering (verify against the staged verse map).

evidence.translation_difficulty: Generally clear Hebrew with concentrated cruces: 4:3 harmonah (hapax); 5:26 Sikkuth/Kiyyun (MT vocalisation vs LXX Moloch/Raiphan, the form Acts 7:42-43 quotes); 6:10 mesarfo (hapax); 6:12 'plow with oxen' (a widely adopted redivision ba-baqar yam); 7:7-8 anak (plumb line or tin, a disputed lexeme); 7:14 the verbless 'I (am/was) no prophet'; 8:8 / 9:5 the Nile comparison; and 9:11-12, where MT 'possess the remnant of Edom' stands against LXX 'the rest of mankind may seek', the form Acts 15:16-17 cites. Numbering is identity MT=WEB.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Patterned oracles against the nations with the 'three transgressions, four' formula (1:3-2:16), didactic disputation by rhetorical questions (3:3-8), hymn fragments set inside prose (4:13; 5:8-9; 9:5-6), a qinah (5:1-3), a covenant-curse recital with refrain (4:6-11), woe oracles (5:18; 6:1), five vision reports (7:1-9; 8:1-3; 9:1-4) interrupted by a third-person biographical narrative (7:10-17), and a salvation epilogue (9:11-15).
evidence.prophecy: Oracular throughout with usable onset signals ('hear this word' 3:1, 4:1, 5:1; 'woe' 5:18, 6:1; 'thus the Lord YHWH showed me' 7:1, 4, 7; 8:1); the eschatological restoration 9:11-15 and the day-of-YHWH reversal 5:18-20 carry the interpretive load, and the internal seams of 3-6 (the 5:1-17 chiasm) turn on judgment.
evidence.connections: 1:2 = Joel 3:16 and 9:13 <-> Joel 3:18 (the Joel-Amos seam); 9:12 Edom <-> Obad (the Amos-Obadiah seam); 5:25-27 <-> Acts 7:42-43; 9:11-12 <-> Acts 15:16-17; 4:11 <-> Gen 19; 2:9-10 exodus and Amorites; 3:2 <-> Deut 7:6; 5:21-24 <-> Isa 1:11-17, Hos 6:6, Mic 6:6-8; 7:10-17 <-> 1 Kgs 12:25-13:34 (Bethel); 4:13 / 5:8 / 9:6 <-> Job 9:8-9, 38:31 (Pleiades, Orion); 8:9 in crucifixion-darkness reception.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported neutrally: 9:11-12 as cited in Acts 15 (Gentile inclusion) rests on the LXX form, so the MT/LXX divergence is itself a reception issue; 3:6 ('does disaster befall a city unless YHWH has done it') is a standing theodicy passage; 5:21-24 is a charter text in liberation and social-justice theology; 3:7 is used in prophetic-authority claims by some movements (an Adventist reading among them); the tense of 7:14 decides Amos's self-understanding of the prophetic office.

books.boundary_risk: Breaking the eight-nation sequence of 1:3-2:16 unevenly or detaching 2:6-16 (Israel) from the pattern; splitting a hymn fragment from its oracle (4:12 / 4:13; 5:7-9; 9:5-6); cutting the Amaziah narrative 7:10-17 so that the third vision (7:7-9) and the fourth (8:1-3) lose their frame; and dividing 9:11-15 so that 9:11-12 (the Acts 15 span) sits apart from 9:13-15.
books.uncertainty: connections could be argued to 3 on the strength of the two Acts citations and the Twelve catchwords; scored 2 because they are localised and text-signalled rather than diffuse.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Twenty-one verses that share vv 1-9 nearly verbatim with Jer 49:7-22 (vv 1-4 ~= Jer 49:14-16; vv 5-6 ~= Jer 49:9-10; v 8 ~= Jer 49:7), with the direction of dependence unsettled; v 20 is a recognised crux ('the exiles of this host', ha-chel ha-zeh, and the place-name Sepharad); v 7 mazor ('trap' or 'wound', disputed); v 16 whose 'you' drank; v 21 moshi'im 'saviours' (MT) vs LXX 'those who have been saved'. Numbering identity; single chapter.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: One oracle against Edom in poetry, moving from judgment (1-14) through the day of YHWH (15-16) to restoration (17-21); the genre is routine, and the only form shift is the prose-like territorial list of 19-20.
evidence.prophecy: An oracle against a nation whose pivot at v 15 ('the day of YHWH is near upon all the nations') is contested: many editors read 15b with 14 and 15a with 16, so the seam between the Edom-specific and the universal sections turns on judgment; 17-21 is predictive restoration ending in 'the kingdom shall be YHWH's'.
evidence.connections: vv 1-9 <-> Jer 49:7-22 (shared text); v 17 <-> Joel 2:32 ('as YHWH has said'); Amos 9:12 immediately precedes with the Edom catchword; Edom/Esau <-> Gen 25, 27, 36 and Deut 23:7; vv 10-14 <-> Ps 137:7, Lam 4:21-22, Ezek 25:12-14, 35; Isa 34, 63:1-6; Mal 1:2-5; v 15 <-> Joel's day of YHWH; v 21 <-> Rev 11:15. For a 21-verse book the connections are the chunking context.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Little doctrinal contest: the Edom/Esau typology feeds the election discussion via Mal 1:2-3 and Rom 9:13 only indirectly; v 21 'saviours on Mount Zion' has a messianic reception among some Jewish and Christian readers; the book's position differs between the MT order of the Twelve (after Amos) and the LXX order (after Joel), a fact of transmission.

books.boundary_risk: Either fragmenting a 21-verse poem into rows too small to be units or making it one whole-book row without disclosure; placing the v 15 pivot on the wrong side (15a / 15b); cutting vv 1-9 from vv 10-14 in a way that hides the Jer 49 parallel span; and detaching 19-21 as a mere list.
extra_scrutiny_focus: vv 17-21 restoration and the Joel 2:32 echo
books.uncertainty: The Jer 49 verse equivalences are from memory and should be checked against the closed Jer corpus rows if the seam is disputed; no other uncertainty.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Late, plain narrative Hebrew; numbering diverges once: MT 2:1 = WEB 1:17 (MT 2:2-11 = WEB 2:1-10). Minor cruces: 3:3 'a city great to God'; 3:4 forty days (LXX three); 4:6 qiqayon (hapax; the Jerome-Augustine 'gourd vs ivy' exchange); 1:17-2:1 dag / dagah gender shift; 4:11 'right hand from left'.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Prose narrative in four scenes with an embedded thanksgiving psalm (2:2-9) whose insertion or integration is debated, a quoted credo (4:2), a royal decree (3:7-9) and a closing rhetorical question (4:10-11); the genre seams at 2:1 / 2:2 and 2:9 / 2:10 are the only difficult ones.
evidence.prophecy: A single five-word oracle (3:4 'forty days and Nineveh is overthrown') in a book about a prophet rather than a book of oracles; boundaries are narrative and text-signalled.
evidence.connections: 4:2 = Joel 2:13 <-> Exod 34:6-7 (the credo, reversed in Nah 1:2-3, Jonah's Nineveh counterpart in the Twelve); 2 Kgs 14:25 (Jonah ben Amittai); Matt 12:39-41, 16:4, Luke 11:29-32 (the sign of Jonah); the psalm's phrase-mosaic from Pss 18, 30, 31, 42, 69, 120; 3:9 <-> Joel 2:14 ('who knows'); 4:3, 8 <-> 1 Kgs 19:4 (Elijah's death-wish); Jer 18:7-8 (the relenting principle); Gen 10:11-12 (Nineveh).
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported neutrally: historicity is a live divide (historical narrative for many conservative Protestant, Catholic and Orthodox readers, often citing Matt 12:40; didactic parable for most critical and mainline readers); 'three days and three nights' (1:17) figures in chronology debates about the crucifixion-resurrection interval; read liturgically at Yom Kippur afternoon in Judaism and in full at the Orthodox Holy Saturday vesperal liturgy.

books.boundary_risk: Treating the psalm 2:2-9 as its own row while the narrative frame 2:1 and 2:10 belongs on both sides of it; and mis-keying the 1:17 / 2:1 MT-WEB zone so the fish verse migrates chapters between witnesses.
books.uncertainty: None material; lowest total in the batch (8) alongside Lam.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Three stretches are held among the most corrupt in the Twelve: 1:10-16 (the town-name lament, whose wordplays are emended in nearly every edition), 2:6-11 (the disputation: 2:7 'is it said, O house of Jacob'; 2:8 'yesterday my people rose up as an enemy'; 2:9-10) and 6:9-16 ('hear the rod and who appointed it' 6:9; 6:10; 6:14 yeshach, hapax). Others: 4:8 Migdal-eder; 5:1 (MT 4:14) titgodedi bat-gedud; 5:5 (MT 5:4) seven shepherds, eight princes; 7:11-12; 7:19. Numbering diverges: MT 4:14 = WEB 5:1 (MT 5:1-14 = WEB 5:2-15).
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Judgment and salvation alternate in blocks with unmarked seams: theophany (1:2-7), paronomastic lament (1:8-16), woe oracle (2:1-5), disputation (2:6-11), shepherd oracle (2:12-13, held misplaced by many), leader indictments (3), Zion eschatology (4:1-5), a chain of 'now' oracles (4:9; 4:11; 5:1), the Bethlehem ruler oracle (5:2-5a), remnant sayings (5:7-9), purge (5:10-15), covenant lawsuit (6:1-8), city indictment (6:9-16), lament (7:1-7) and a prophetic liturgy of confidence, prayer and hymn (7:8-20).
evidence.prophecy: Predictive and eschatological material dominates 4-5 and 7:8-20 (4:1-5 Zion; 4:10 Babylon; 5:2-5a Bethlehem; 5:7-15; 7:11-13), and the sub-division of 4-5 (the attah series 4:9, 4:11, 5:1 as three units or one; where 5:2-6 begins and ends) is decided by judgment; 3:12 is the one oracle quoted by name elsewhere (Jer 26:18).
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported neutrally: 5:2 (MT 5:1) 'whose goings forth are from of old, from days of eternity' is read as the pre-existent Messiah born at Bethlehem in Christian tradition and as the antiquity of the Davidic line in Jewish and historical reading; 4:1-5 sits in millennial/dispensational schemes for some and in ecclesial-fulfilment readings for others; 6:6-8 is a standing text in cult-versus-ethics discussion across traditions; 7:18-20 is the Tashlikh liturgy in Judaism; the unity of 4-5 and of 7:8-20 is a critical rather than an ecclesial dispute.

books.boundary_risk: Cutting the 4:1-5 unit at 4:3 or 4:4 (the Isaiah parallel ends at 4:3 while Mic's unit runs to 4:5); mis-seaming 4:14 / 5:1 across the MT-WEB offset so the Bethlehem oracle's onset (WEB 5:2 = MT 5:1) is keyed wrongly; imposing a structure on 1:10-16 or 2:6-11 that the corrupt text does not support; detaching 2:12-13 as an intrusion by editorial theory rather than text signal; and splitting the 7:8-20 liturgy into speaker-fragments without disclosure.
books.uncertainty: translation_difficulty could be argued at 2 because the corruption is clustered in three stretches; scored 3 under the upward rule since those stretches are exactly where boundaries fall.

evidence.translation_difficulty: 1:2-8 is a broken alphabetic acrostic (alef through kaf with irregular lines), and whether to restore it by emendation is a standing text-critical question that fixes where the hymn ends; 1:9-2:2 alternates second-person addressees (feminine Nineveh vs Judah) in an obscure text (1:10 'entangled thorns, drunk with their drink'; 1:12 'though complete and so many'); 2:7 (MT 2:8) hutsav ('Huzzab' or a verb); 2:10 (MT 2:11) buqah u-mevuqah u-mevullaqah; 3:17 minnezarim / taphsarim (Assyrian loanwords). Numbering diverges: MT 2:1 = WEB 1:15 (MT 2:2-14 = WEB 2:1-13).
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: A theophanic hymn with partial acrostic (1:2-8), alternating oracles to Judah and Nineveh (1:9-2:2), a battle vision in vivid present tense (2:3-13), a woe oracle with harlot taunt (3:1-7), a comparison taunt on Thebes (3:8-13) and a locust-simile dirge (3:14-19); forty-seven verses, all poetry, with the 1:9-2:2 seams marked only by gender and number of address.
evidence.prophecy: A massa (1:1) against Nineveh throughout, predictive of its fall (612 BCE); 1:15 (MT 2:1) is a salvation word to Judah inside the judgment; boundaries in 1:9-2:2 turn on addressee assignment, elsewhere on scene change.
evidence.connections: 1:2-3 <-> Exod 34:6-7 (the credo in reverse order from Jonah 4:2, its Twelve-counterpart on Nineveh; also Mic 7:18-20 immediately before); 1:15 (MT 2:1) ~= Isa 52:7 (the herald's feet; Rom 10:15); 1:4 <-> Isa 33:9; 2:11-13 lions <-> Isa 5:29; 3:1 'city of bloods' <-> Ezek 22:2, 24:6; 3:4-5 harlot <-> Isa 47, Rev 17-18 imagery; 3:8 Thebes <-> Ezek 30:14-16; Zeph 2:13-15 (Nineveh); 1:3 storm-theophany <-> Ps 18, 97.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Seldom a site of doctrinal division; the vengeance theology of 1:2-3 is a passage readers struggle with (reception ranging from Marcionite rejection to its use as the counterpart of Jonah's mercy), and the book is nearly absent from Christian lectionaries; the acrostic dispute is scholarly rather than ecclesial.

books.boundary_risk: Ending the hymn at 1:8 vs 1:10 or 1:11 depending on the acrostic theory; assigning 1:9-2:2 verses to the wrong addressee and so to the wrong unit; and mis-keying the 1:15 / 2:1 MT-WEB zone so the Judah salvation word migrates between chapters in the two witnesses.
books.uncertainty: The 3 for translation is driven by the proportion of a 47-verse book under textual dispute (roughly 1:2-14, 2:7-13, 3:15-19) and by the acrostic question's direct bearing on a seam, not by absolute crux density comparable to Hosea or Ezekiel; 2 is the alternative reading.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Ch 3 is an archaic theophany psalm with musical rubrics (3:1 al shigyonoth; selah at 3:3, 9, 13; 3:19b lamnatseach) and a run of obscure lines (3:4 'rays/horns from his hand'; 3:9 'sworn were the rods of the word, selah', among the most obscure verses in the prophets; 3:13-14; 3:16-17). Elsewhere: 1:9 megammat (hapax); 1:12 a tiqqun soferim ('we shall not die' for 'you'); 2:4 with MT be-emunato 'by his faithfulness' against LXX ek pisteos mou 'by my faith', the form the NT quotes; 2:5 'wine' (MT) vs 'wealth' (1QpHab); 2:15-16 he'arel / hera'el (a 1QpHab variant); 2:17 K/Q. Numbering identity MT=WEB.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: In 56 verses: a complaint-answer dialogue (1:2-4 lament; 1:5-11 oracle; 1:12-17 lament; 2:1 watch; 2:2-5 answer), five woe oracles (2:6-20) with liturgical refrains (2:14; 2:20), and then a complete psalm form inside a prophetic book (3:1 superscription; 3:2 petition; 3:3-15 archaic theophany; 3:16-19a response; 3:19b subscription) marked by selah; the rubric seams are text signals, but the poetry of 3 is the most archaic in the Twelve.
evidence.prophecy: The Chaldean oracle (1:5-11), the vision to be written and awaited (2:2-3), the woes (2:6-20) and the theophany (3:3-15) are all oracular, but onsets are well signalled ('how long' 1:2; 'look' 1:5; 'and YHWH answered' 2:2; 'woe' x5; 3:1); the one contested seam is where the divine answer ends and the woes begin (2:4 / 2:5 / 2:6).
evidence.connections: 2:4 <-> Rom 1:17, Gal 3:11, Heb 10:38 (with 2:3 in Heb 10:37, LXX form); 1:5 <-> Acts 13:41 (LXX 'you scoffers'); 2:14 ~= Isa 11:9; 2:20 <-> Zeph 1:7, Zech 2:13; 3:3-15 <-> Deut 33:2, Judg 5:4-5, Ps 68:7-8, Ps 77:16-19 (the archaic theophany tradition); 3:19 ~= Ps 18:33 / 2 Sam 22:34; 2:18-19 idol polemic <-> Isa 44:9-20, Jer 10:1-16; 2:1 <-> Isa 21:8; 1QpHab (the Qumran pesher) as a reception witness on 1:1-2:20.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reported neutrally: 2:4 is the proof text at the centre of the justification debate (Luther's reading against the Council of Trent's, the Joint Declaration of 1999 as a later stage), and its three text forms (his faithfulness / my faith / by faith) are read differently by Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant exegetes and within the pistis Christou discussion; 3:2 in the Old Greek ('in the midst of two living creatures you will be known') underlies the ox-and-ass nativity tradition, and Habakkuk's prayer is Ode 4 of the Orthodox canon; 3:13 'your anointed' has messianic and royal readings; 1:13 is a standing theodicy passage.

books.boundary_risk: Cutting inside the complaint-answer dialogue so that a lament loses its reply (1:2-4 from 1:5-11; 1:12-2:1 from 2:2-5); placing 2:4-5 with the answer or with the woes; separating the psalm's superscription 3:1 or subscription 3:19b from the poem, or cutting the theophany 3:3-15 from the 3:16-19a response; and breaking the five-woe series unevenly.
books.uncertainty: ecclesial_contestedness at 3 rests almost entirely on 2:4 and 3:2 in a 56-verse book; if the consolidator weights breadth over depth, 2 is the alternative. Qumran variant details (2:5, 2:15-16) are from memory of 1QpHab.
